Five Colombian Cities Rank Among World's Most Congested According to TomTom Traffic Index

2026-09-08 El Colombiano TomTom Traffic Index 2025, Colombia, Bogotá, Medellín, Cali, Barranquilla, Cartagena, traffic congestion, Graphisoft, BIM, infrastructure planning, road congestion
Read the source article

Quick summary

The TomTom Traffic Index 2025 reveals that four Colombian cities — Bogotá, Medellín, Cali, and Barranquilla — rank among the 20 most congested in the world, with Bogotá leading at 69.6% congestion, underscoring a national challenge in urban mobility planning.

Key takeaways

  • Bogotá recorded the highest congestion level among Colombian cities at 69.6%, meaning travel times were on average 69.6% longer than free-flow conditions
  • Medellín followed at 66.9%, Cali at 65.6%, Barranquilla at 62.8%, and Cartagena at 57.7%
  • Four Colombian cities placed among the 20 most congested cities globally in the TomTom Traffic Index 2025
  • All five major Colombian cities exceeded 57% congestion, well above the global average
  • Graphisoft identifies five keys for modernizing road infrastructure: integrate information from the start, simulate before building, detect errors early, plan for future growth, and strengthen digital talent
  • The use of open standards like IFC is recommended to ensure information accessibility across all project stakeholders
